sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Weighted Chin Up is an advanced vertical pulling exercise that adds external load to the bodyweight chin up using a dip belt, weight vest, or similar.

Pulling with a supinated (palms-in) grip places a large stimulus on the lats and biceps while heavily recruiting the upper back.

It is one of the most effective exercises for building upper-body pulling strength, arm size, and back thickness.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Builds maximal upper-body pulling strength
- Heavy recruitment of the lats and biceps
- Strengthens the grip and forearms
- Improves scapular control and shoulder health
- Scalable load makes long-term progression easy
- Transfers to deadlifts, rows, and other pulling lifts
- Minimal equipment needed

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps Brachii

Secondary: Rhomboids, Middle/Lower Trapezius, Rear Deltoids, Forearms, Core

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Attach weight securely using a dip belt, weight vest, or held dumbbell.
2. Stand under a sturdy pull-up bar.
3. Chalk up or dry your hands if needed.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Grip the pull-up bar with palms facing you (supinated).
2. Hands roughly shoulder-width apart or slightly closer.
3. Hang with arms extended, shoulders packed, and core braced.

sections.heading: Pull
sections.content:
1. Initiate the pull by depressing the shoulder blades.
2. Drive the elbows down and back, leading with the chest.
3. Pull until the chin clears the bar.

sections.heading: Return and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Lower the body under control to a full hang.
2. Keep tension in the lats and shoulders at the bottom.
3. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, adjusting load as needed.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Kipping or using leg drive instead of strict form
- Incomplete range of motion at the top or bottom
- Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
- Flaring the elbows out instead of driving down
- Adding weight before mastering strict bodyweight reps
- Letting the load swing during the rep
- Losing core bracing during the set

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Sturdy pull-up bar
- Dip belt with chain, weight vest, or dumbbell between the feet
- Weight plates appropriate for your strength
- Chalk for grip (optional)
- Optional: Lifting straps for very heavy sets
- Optional: Box or step to reach the bar

sections.heading: Weight Attachment
sections.content:
1. Load plates onto the dip belt and secure the belt around the waist.
2. Alternatively, pinch a dumbbell between the feet or wear a weight vest.
3. Start with light load and build up gradually.
4. Confirm all attachments are secure before leaving the floor.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Grip: Supinated (palms facing you), shoulder-width or slightly closer.
2. Body: Feet together or slightly crossed, hips slightly in front of the bar.
3. Torso: Ribs down, core braced, slight posterior pelvic tilt.
4. Shoulders: Packed and down at the start of each rep.
5. Head: Neutral, eyes forward or slightly up.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Bodyweight Chin Up: Unloaded variation
- Weighted Pull Up: Pronated grip variation
- Lat Pulldown: Cable variation for easier loading
- Band-Assisted Chin Up: Assisted variation for beginners
- Inverted Row: Horizontal pulling alternative
- Barbell Row: Free-weight pulling alternative

sections.heading: Weighted Chin Up Variations
sections.content:
Weighted Chin Up: Described here
Weighted Pull Up: Pronated grip for more lat emphasis
Weighted Neutral-Grip Chin Up: Palms facing each other
Weighted Close-Grip Chin Up: Narrow grip for more bicep
Tempo Weighted Chin Up: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy
Pause Weighted Chin Up: Pause at the top for more tension

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Pain: Reduce range at the bottom and keep shoulders packed
Elbow Pain: Try a neutral or wider grip
Grip Issues: Use chalk or lifting straps
Can Not Do Bodyweight Chin Up: Use band-assisted or negatives first
Load Too Light: Add more plates to the belt
Load Too Heavy: Reduce load or drop to bodyweight reps
Beginners: Master strict bodyweight chin ups before adding load
